answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network routes game-theoretic multi-agent audits across a topological cut prism, forcing independent clusters to sign findings with a cryptographic quill. If colluding nodes forge identities to breach the cut, auditors cross-verify sparse graph cuts and trigger stake slashing. This plunges an adversary’s payoff to its economic nadir and imposes superlinear attacker cost scaling with identity count.
